findings.reason: the section must cite the existing owner and check whether its three hand-over measures already hold, rather than dispatch a node to rebuild them.
findings.text: §5 presents "let a lane declare where its work goes when it is spent … resolved at dispatch when the primary is held" and "spec level can name a backend" as new machinery, but `resolve_budget_fallback` (routing.py:379) already returns a held backend's declared fallback and refuses when none is declared, and dispatch already substitutes it at dispatch.py:6836; `by_spec_level.<level>.backend` already resolves a backend at cli.py:2490 — the plan's §5 measures may already be satisfied by code in the tree, the same currency-audit pattern the plan applies to §2 and §3

findings.reason: the measure as written cannot be satisfied by a channel the plan does not name, and would otherwise ship a second delivery mechanism beside the one that provably does not reach workers.
findings.text: §17's measure "an overrun messages the worker and terminates nothing" requires delivering a message to a live worker, but names no channel and does not reconcile with the measured fact that a CLI-launched print-mode worker has no turn in which to receive one (the same workstation measured 0 deliveries in 3,949 worker streams); the honest change is to extend the existing peer/message surface and state whether it can reach a worker mid-turn rather than add a parallel delivery path

findings.reason: the section should extend the existing endpoints reader (and the producer surface that consumes it) rather than fork a second one, so a lane drop is observed once at the owner and not by two readers that can drift.
findings.text: §18's measure "the lane's availability is observed once, at the producer, and delivered to every follower" proposes a new producer-side reader of the endpoints document, but that read is already owned by `serving_origin.py:85` against the `endpoints_document` field declared in `_flight_schema.py:289`; the plan itself notes the routing pre-flight already reports serving state "by a better route"

findings.reason: the section must account for the added verb at cli_options and the added write path at mcp_views, since the rubric holds any section that grows an interface family to name what it retires or why nothing can be.
findings.text: §15 asks for a new `crew` verb that "records an additional exclusive path on a live run" and §14 asks for a `section_declarations` write path on the MCP surface (public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23); neither section names an interface it retires or merges, nor states why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — every section lands its behaviour in an existing owning module (routing.py, dispatch.py, recovery.py, ticker.py, reports.py); no new module is proposed that would spread one behaviour across several single-call wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 proposes a producer-side watcher over the lane's endpoints document, a reader already owned by reckon/crew/serving_origin.py:85 against the `endpoints_document` field declared at reckon/_flight_schema.py:289.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §15 adds a new `crew` verb to grant a scope extension and §14 adds a `section_declarations` write path, and neither section names what it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §5 proposes a held-lane declared fallback and a by_spec_level entry that names a backend, both of which already exist in the tree (`resolve_budget_fallback` at reckon/crew/routing.py:379, called from reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6836; `by_spec_level.<level>.backend` at reckon/cli.py:2490) and neither is cited by §5.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §17 adds a "message is delivered to the running worker" measure without naming the existing delivery channel or reconciling it with the measured fact that messages to headless print-mode workers do not arrive.
